user_observation.research_use: Treat sequential nome numbering as a topology/search signal to be tested inside the already-active reverse-only Tranception pass, not as proof of a ritual sequence by itself.

LE16.evidence_summary: UCL records Djedet/Mendes as Lower Egyptian nome 16 and the Banebdjedet sanctuary with four ba/souls including Osiris. IFAO scholarship records late Osirian relic lists assigning phallus and backbone to Mendes and Edfu material linking a phallus and an offering vessel containing the sexual organ with Mendes/Banebdjedet.

LE17.important_correction: UCL verifies Semabehdet as the principal city of Lower Egyptian nome 17 but lists a major Amun temple and has no surviving White Chapel deity entry. Secondary Egyptological literature connects a northern Behdet and Horus Behdetite with this Delta nome, but this should not yet be promoted to a fully verified main-cult identity.

LE18.important_temporal_note: UCL notes that territory later constituting nome 18 had earlier belonged to nome 13; therefore the 16-17-18 administrative sequence is not a timeless invariant across all Egyptian periods.

mendes_strengthening.reason: Mendes remains independently strong even if the 16-17-18 ritual-sequence hypothesis fails. Its evidentiary weight comes from convergence of nome geography, Banebdjedet/Osiris ba theology, Osirian phallus+backbone relic geography, Edfu offering scenes, Mendesian papyrus theology, priestly funerary context, and the documented CG53469 phallus sheath.
not_dependent_on: Horus Behdetite being conclusively the main deity of nome 17
Bastet forming a ritual triad with Osiris and Horus
the numbers 16-17-18 encoding a hidden prophecy

six_direction_pass: BACK: from CG53469/Mendes toward earlier cult geography
FORWARD: test whether ancient-source geography independently returns Mendes
LEFT: inspect nome 17 / Behdet as an adjacent dynastic-Horus continuation candidate
RIGHT: inspect nome 18 / Bubastis as an adjacent Bastet/feline protective continuation candidate
FORWARD_AGAIN: ask whether 16->17->18 predicts a ritual sequence in primary temple/relic texts
BACK_AGAIN: if not, return to Mendes and preserve only the independently supported nodes

canonical_line: 16-17-18 IS A ROAD SIGN, NOT YET A RITUAL SCRIPT. MENDES REMAINS STRONG EVEN IF THE NEIGHBOURING-NOME HYPOTHESIS FAILS.
